title: Machine-learning metabolomics distinguishes SARS-CoV-2, influenza A and RSV from respiratory swabs
summary: Untargeted metabolomics and machine learning identified upper-respiratory-swab signatures for SARS-CoV-2 positivity, followed by targeted LC-MS/MS profiling. Across 1,226 samples (521 SARS-CoV-2-positive, 97 influenza A, 96 RSV, 211 other respiratory viruses and 301 virus-negative), the best SARS-CoV-2 LightGBM model had AUC 0.99, sensitivity 0.96 and specificity 0.95. Separate models reported AUC 0.97 for influenza A and 0.99 for RSV. The top-ranked SARS-CoV-2 features included 3-oxo-heneicosanoic acid and 2-(4-hydroxyphenyl) ethanol.
ai_technology: Light Gradient Boosting Machine and other machine-learning classifiers applied to mass-spectrometry metabolomics
organization: British Columbia Centre for Disease Control Public Health Laboratory; University of British Columbia; Stanford University School of Medicine; Stanford Health Care; Chan Zuckerberg Biohub

evidence.tested: Separate models reported AUC 0.97 for influenza A and 0.99 for RSV.
evidence.unknown: This is an assay-validation study using stored respiratory specimens, not a prospective clinical-impact trial. Results establish classification in the studied cohorts and do not show improved patient outcomes or routine deployment. The source notes unresolved oxo-position/isomer assignment for several features. The metabolite signals are candidate host-response markers, not proof of virus-specific causal biology.
evidence.ai_role: Machine-learning feature ranking identified metabolite signatures in untargeted profiles; the team adapted candidate signatures to targeted LC-MS/MS, and evaluated classification in respiratory-virus sample cohorts. The models supplied the sample-level classification and feature ranking, while mass spectrometry measured the metabolites.
